item.title: Justin Daerr
item.description: On May 26th, 1967, my father was serving in Vietnam as a Lieutenant in the United States Marine Corps when he was severely wounded. He was 22-years-old. He had to spend the remainder of that year in various hospitals undergoing multiple surgeries. He lost all flexion in one of his ankles, lost sight in one eye, lost part of his hearing, was covered in shrapnel and later in life suffered additional severe health issues. item.title: Ken Rideout
item.description: The first thing I do in the morning is go for a run. It’s never a negotiation. I’ve never woken up and thought to myself that I don’t feel like doing it today. It’s just never happened. I get up and do it because I know the kind of depression I’ll carry around with me the rest of the day if I don't get that endorphin rush in the morning. It’s almost like a necessary evil. People think I’m crazy when I tell them I run 10 to 15 miles per day, especially when it’s done before I go into the office.
